script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. October 3rd, 2026. Another Friday, right?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。2026年10月3日。また金曜日ですね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Morning, Alex. Yes, it is.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。そうね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Welcome to The Daily Tanu-chan Show. It's a bit overcast today, isn't it? Feels cooler than yesterday.
script.ja: ザ・デイリー・タヌちゃんショーへようこそ。今日は少し曇ってますね？昨日より涼しい気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yeah, they said it'll be around 22 degrees high. Looks like rain later, too.
script.ja: ええ、最高気温は22度くらいだって。後で雨も降りそうね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I definitely need this coffee. Couldn't sleep last night. My little one was up.
script.ja: このコーヒー、絶対必要です。昨夜は眠れませんでした。うちの子が起きてて。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Oh, that's tough.
script.ja: あら、大変ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Did you see that news about kanji? How one character can have five different pronunciations?
script.ja: 漢字のニュース見ました？一つの文字に5つも読み方があるって。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. That's always been the hardest part for learners, I think.
script.ja: 見たわ。学習者にとってはいつも一番難しいところだと思う。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I remember when I was a *fledgling* English speaker, I thought our writing system was so hard. But Japanese is next level sometimes.
script.ja: ええ、僕がまだ英語学習の駆け出しだった頃、僕らの文字体系はすごく難しいって思ってました。でも日本語は時々次のレベルですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: A *fledgling* speaker? You mean like, new or just starting out?
script.ja: 『フレッジリング』スピーカー？初心者とか、始めたばかりってこと？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, exactly! Like a baby bird learning to fly. Is that what it means?
script.ja: ええ、まさに！飛ぶことを学ぶひな鳥みたいな。そういう意味ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Pretty much. Someone new to something, still a bit shaky.
script.ja: 大体そうね。何かに不慣れで、まだ少し不安定な人って感じ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Speaking of history, they found a samurai sword in America. Yoshida Shoin's, apparently.
script.ja: 歴史の話だけど、アメリカで侍の刀が見つかったそうよ。吉田松陰のものらしいわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Wow, really? That's kind of amazing, actually. How does something like that even end up over there?
script.ja: わあ、本当ですか？それ、ちょっとすごいですね。どうやってそんなものが向こうに渡ったんでしょう？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Probably during the Meiji Restoration, when many left Japan. Things got complicated back then.
script.ja: おそらく明治維新の頃、多くの人が日本を離れた時期ね。あの頃は色々複雑だったから。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My kid is crawling everywhere now. Can't take my eyes off them. Sometimes I just feel so *demoralized* by the lack of sleep.
script.ja: うちの子、今あちこちハイハイしてます。もう目が離せない。時々、睡眠不足で本当に意気消沈しちゃいます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Demoralized? You mean like really tired, or something else?
script.ja: 意気消沈？すごく疲れているってこと？それとも何か違う意味？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Well, yeah, tired, but also just feeling a bit defeated, you know? Like I'm losing the battle against exhaustion.
script.ja: ええ、疲れてるのもそうですが、ちょっと打ち負かされた気分っていうか。疲労との戦いに負けてる感じ、分かります？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Ah, defeated. Yes, that's what demoralized means. Losing confidence or hope.
script.ja: ああ、打ち負かされた感じね。そうね、それが意気消沈するっていう意味よ。自信や希望を失うことね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They're hiking visa fees for residency from Thursday, apparently.
script.ja: どうやら木曜日から在留ビザの手数料が上がるそうよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that. That's not going to change at my office, thankfully. Most of our clients are domestic.
script.ja: ああ、知りませんでした。幸い、うちのオフィスでは影響なさそうです。ほとんどのお客さんは国内なので。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It'll affect some people for sure. My son's friend is applying for permanent residency next year.
script.ja: 何人かの人には確実に影響するわね。うちの息子の友達が来年、永住権を申請するのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, speaking of tomorrow, I just remembered, October 4th is イワシの日, Sardine Day.
script.ja: ああ、明日といえば、今思い出しましたけど、10月4日はイワシの日です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Sardine Day? Oh, right. 'I-wa-shi'. The date sounds like it.
script.ja: イワシの日？ああ、そうね。「イ（1）ワ（0）シ（4）」。日付が語呂合わせになってるのね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, for promoting how good sardines are for you. I should probably eat more of them.
script.ja: ええ、イワシがいかに体に良いかをアピールするためらしいです。もっと食べるべきですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I actually made some sardine pasta for meal prep this weekend. Wanted to try something new.
script.ja: 実は週末のミールプレップで、イワシのパスタを作ったのよ。何か新しいものを試してみたくて。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? Was it good? I always think about meal prep, but then the weekend comes and I just want to relax.
script.ja: おお、本当ですか？美味しかったですか？僕もいつもミールプレップを考えるんですが、週末になるとただリラックスしたいって思っちゃって。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It was pretty good. And it saves so much time during the week, especially with the kids' after-school activities.
script.ja: 結構美味しかったわ。それに、週の間はすごく時間が節約できるのよ、特に子供たちの習い事があるとね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Well, I guess I should try to get some sardines then. Maybe a bit more sleep too.
script.ja: まあ、じゃあイワシを手に入れようかな。もう少し睡眠もね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good luck with that. Have a good one, Alex.
script.ja: 頑張ってね。良い週末を、アレックス。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You too, Sarah. See you Monday.
script.ja: サラさんも。また月曜日に。

wikipedia.description: 1985年、「い（1）わ（0）し（4）」の語呂合わせから、大阪府多獲性魚有効利用検討会（大坂おさなか健康食品協議会）が制定。栄養豊富なイワシをPRするのが目的。
